---
title: "Post-war quarterly data"
---

Table 8 repeats the estimation on quarterly data from 1948 to 2015, so
that the result does not rest on the Great Depression years. With time
aggregation the decision frequency $h$ is the number of decisions in a
quarter, chosen on the grid 1 to 4. Without it $h = 1$: the agent
decides once a quarter.

The quarterly panel follows the model's conventions. Prices and
dividends are real. The quarterly dividend is the trailing four-quarter
real sum divided by four, the usual treatment of the seasonal and
payment-timing noise in quarterly dividends, and the price-dividend
ratio is price over that one-quarter flow because the model's
time-aggregated moment sums dividends over one sampling interval. The
mean log P/D therefore sits about $\log 4$ above the annual one.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
from great_tables import GT

from geap.lrr.estimation import estimate_bky, load_quarterly, table8_frame

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")


def fmt_params(gt, tab):
    """Two decimals for the large parameters, four for the rest, scientific for sigma_w."""
    idx = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(tab["parameter"])}
    two = [idx[n] for n in ("gamma", "psi", "phi_d", "phi_d_sigma", "h", "J") if n in idx]
    three = [idx[n] for n in ("rho_d", "p") if n in idx]
    sci = [idx[n] for n in ("sigma_w",) if n in idx]
    four = [i for i in range(len(tab)) if i not in two + three + sci]
    num = [c for c in tab.columns if c != "parameter"]
    return (
        gt.fmt_number(columns=num, rows=four, decimals=4)
        .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=two, decimals=2)
        .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=three, decimals=3)
        .fmt_scientific(columns=num, rows=sci, decimals=2)
        .sub_missing(missing_text="")
    )


quarterly = load_quarterly()
print(f"n = {len(quarterly)} quarters, {quarterly['date'].dt.year.min()} to {quarterly['date'].dt.year.max()}")
```

## Table 8

```{python}
ta = estimate_bky(quarterly, n_starts=3)
no_ta = estimate_bky(quarterly, h=1, n_starts=6)
tab8 = table8_frame(ta, no_ta)
fmt_params(
    GT(tab8)
    .tab_header(title="Table 8. Model estimates using post-war quarterly data")
    .tab_spanner(label="Time aggregation", columns=["ta_hat", "ta_se", "ta_paper", "ta_paper_se"])
    .tab_spanner(label="No time aggregation", columns=["nota_hat", "nota_se", "nota_paper", "nota_paper_se"])
    .cols_label(parameter="", ta_hat="estimate", ta_se="SE", ta_paper="paper", ta_paper_se="paper SE",
                nota_hat="estimate", nota_se="SE", nota_paper="paper", nota_paper_se="paper SE")
    .tab_source_note("Parameters are per decision period. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 8."),
    tab8,
).tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
```

::: {.firewall}
Every "paper" column is quoted from Bansal, Kiku, and Yaron (2016),
Table 8. The quarterly panel is rebuilt from the same CRSP, BLS, and
BEA sources as the annual one. The paper does not say how it treats
quarterly dividends; the trailing-sum flow used here matches the
model's mean and volatility of the price-dividend ratio at the paper's
printed vector to within 0.03, and its dividend-growth autocorrelation
of 0.32 sits next to the model's 0.29. The estimates do not reproduce
the paper's contrast. With time aggregation the grid lands on the
paper's two decisions a quarter, but with a risk aversion above the
printed 7.45 and a rejected J-test. Without it the risk aversion sits
near the printed 8.66 and the J-test does not reject. `NUMBERS.md`
lists the open caveats.
:::
